messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency breach detected for route /v1/generate (p95=5.6s > SLO 1.2s). Group: eng-oncall. Auto-run: quick-check. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/ALRT-9876

pagerduty: Incident PD-78231 created and page fired to rotation eng-oncall. Escalation policy: standard.

Tess M: acked. I'm on it, pulling up graphs and logs.

Matt O: acked. I'm here too, looking at tail latency + hotkey patterns. Any region bias?

Tess M: appears concentrated in us-west. p95 jumped around 12:34 UTC then sustained. Error rate not elevated but backend spans taking 2-6s. KV cache eviction rate spiking ~12:35.

Linh R: I'm restarting predictor sidecars in west pool-2 (rolling, 1 pod at a time) to see if long-lived connections are stuck. Command: 
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/predictor-west -n inference
watch -n 1 kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=predictor-west
```

Kara S: adding note: some customers reported UI slow page loads via Intercom — low volume but real. cc @support for customer msgs.

Matt O: digging into autoscaler, saw sudden drop in batch efficiency (batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 tokens) at same time window. Might be request churn causing KV cache miss storms.

incident-bot: quick-check results: CPU and GPU utilization normal; KV cache hit-rate dropped 40%; median seq len unchanged. Suggested mitigation: warm caches and temporarily lower batching threshold to prioritize larger batches.

Tess M: trying a quick cache warm by replaying recent hot prefixes to the cache (non-invasive). Running job: 
```
python infra/tools/warm_cache.py --route /v1/generate --prefixes-file /tmp/hot_prefixes.txt --concurrency 8
```

Linh R: restart progressed: 2/12 pods restarted, no crashloop. Observing slight p95 improvement on restarted nodes.

Matt O: I'm going to nudge autoscaler min replicas + add surge capacity in west for 10m to absorb irregulars. Patch: 
```
kubectl scale deploy predictor-west --replicas=16 -n inference
```

Tess M: pagerduty shows another autopage fired for the same alert (noisy threshold). This is noisy but real signal — likely transient heatwave + cache eviction interaction.

Kara S: support triage: opened a single consolidated ticket for affected customers, low severity but visible slowdown. Notified the largest impacted customer with ETA ~30m.

Matt O: after scale + 6 restarts + cache warm, p95 down to ~1.8s but still above SLO. Continuing monitoring.

Tess M: handing hotseat to Matt O for the next 30m while I jump to a customer call. If p95 remains >2s after 15m, escalate to infra-sre for kernel-side investigation.

Matt O: taking over. I'll keep checking KV eviction, batch size distribution, and autoscaler logs. If we see error-rate growth or 504s, I'll trigger fallback to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive routes. :eyes:

incident-bot: Note: PD-78231 status updated: acknowledged by Tess M, assigned to Matt O. Auto-posting summary to incident channel in 10m.

Kara S: :thumbsup: will update the support ticket with the handoff and current mitigation steps.

Tess M: thanks team — will rejoin if things spike again.
